note: No row drives a GPIO: -csl/-csh on a real port set a pin that may be wired to anything. Every path that reserves the manager calls spi_configure first, which is harmless here - only wkspi uses spi0 on these boards. A transfer used to wait for its completion forever (KWAIT_INFINITY in spi0.c) and hung Discovery_N657, whose SPI4 never completes one; it is now bounded and abandoned cleanly (fixed, ../DEFECTS.md). Why the N657 transfer never completes is still open.

tests.note: argv[1] used to be read before argc was checked: it held whatever an earlier command left there - a garbage manager name on Discovery_N657, a NULL and a HardFault on Nucleo_H743 right after restart (fixed, ../DEFECTS.md)
no GPIO port Z: nothing is written
the configuration is static in wkspi, so the step puts back its default (POL 1, PHA 1, 5 MHz)
before fix/wkspi-unit-range any unit above 3 fell into the default: case and drove spi0, while the report said spi7
the whole value is checked: the uint8_t unit alone would turn 256 into spi0

whatever SPI does on this board, the transfer must answer within its bound (KSPI_TIMEOUT_WRITEREAD, 1 s) rather than hang the console, and a second one must not be refused as busy - the model used to leave vBusy set after a timeout. On Discovery_N657 it answers 'general problem': its SPI4 never completes a transfer (../DEFECTS.md)
needs MOSI wired to MISO on spi0, and a transfer that completes: on Discovery_N657 it hangs the board (../DEFECTS.md)
